nina: FYI the new JS/TS sample app crashes on Deno with "package subpath './internal' not defined by "exports"". Node builds fine. anyone got a neat, minimal fix for dual-pkg + deno?

tor: short answer: publish a tiny deno entrypoint. Node conditional exports don't map 1:1 to Deno.

cass: agreed. practical checklist we've used: 1) build a dist/deno with ESM .js files (no .mjs), 2) add an explicit ./deno export pointing at dist/deno/mod.js, 3) emit deno-friendly d.ts that use .js specifiers or add typesVersions mapping.

nina: for typesVersions, do you mean like mapping "deno/*" to dist/deno/*.d.ts? will that make TS pick up types for import 'pkg/deno'?

tor: yes. example mapping: { "*": { "deno": ["dist/deno/index.d.ts"], "deno/*": ["dist/deno/*.d.ts"] } }. TS will resolve imports to the deno d.ts files.

cass: also be careful with runtime deps: our auth/retry code used node-fetch + AbortController polyfills and that caused token refresh hangs in Fresh. For deno build, avoid node-only polyfills and use a runtime adapter (src/runtime/node.ts + src/runtime/deno.ts) resolved at build time.

nina: is feature-detection (globalThis.fetch) enough or should we prefer build-time selection?

tor: build-time is safer for packaging: bundle a deno artifact that doesn't even include node-fetch. Feature-detect at runtime is OK for single-package builds but leads to unnecessary polyfills being shipped.

cass: small nit on d.ts: ensure your generated declaration files use the same specifiers consumers will import (i.e., ./mod.js) or TS + Deno will complain. We patched our generator to emit .js in import specifiers for the deno bundle.

types-bot: created issue #5001: "sdk: deno entrypoint + typesVersions + runtime adapter for auth/retry + CI deno smoke" https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/5001 :white_check_mark:

nina: cool. i'll open a tiny PR that adds dist/deno, ./deno export, deno d.ts, and a GH action that runs a deno smoke example. thanks!

tor: one more doc note: recommend consumers import from 'redwood-inference/deno' in README to avoid ambiguous subpath resolution. saves support tickets. :+1:
